고급 What you'll learn Understand the three-tier trick — dense weights in RAM, routed experts on disk, optional VRAM tier — and why MoE makes it possible at all Read the benchmark table honestly: which hardware gets 0.1 tok/s, which gets ~2, which gets ~6, and why NVMe bandwidth, not CPU, is the ceiling Know the four gotchas that cost people days: int8 MTP heads, O_DIRECT on the wrong drive, speculative decoding that loses, and SSD wear Get from git clone to a first streamed token on GLM-5.2 or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Decide when Colibrì beats a GGUF-plus-Ollama offload, when to rent a GPU instead, and when a hosted API is simply the right answer On July 1, 2026 a developer publishing as JustVugg pushed a repository with a one-line promise: run frontier MoE models on hardware you already own — pure C, zero deps, experts streamed from disk. The Show HN thread hit 453 points nine days later. By mid-September the project is at 30.8k stars and version 1.11.0, released September 13, added a ninth model family (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 552B) that reads the published checkpoint natively with no conversion step. It is the top AI repository on GitHub's daily trending list as this page is written. The pitch sounds like a trick, and in a sense it is one. This page explains the trick precisely enough that you can predict what it will do on your machine before you download 370 GB.
documents.s: Colibrì: Run a 744B MoE From Your SSD (and What It Really Costs You)

documents.t: A mixture-of-experts model only touches a small slice of its weights per token, so Colibrì keeps the always-used part (attention, embeddings, shared experts) resident in RAM and reads the rarely-used part (the routed experts) from NVMe on demand — trading tokens per second for the ability to run a 744-billion-parameter model on a laptop.

Take GLM-5.2 as the reference case, since it is the model the project was built around: Quantity Value Total parameters 744B Active per token ~40B Dense (always-on) parameters ~17B → ~9.9 GB resident as int4 Routed experts roughly twenty thousand across all layers → ~370 GB on disk as int4 Expert weight that changes token to token (cold) ~11 GB Minimum RAM / comfortable RAM 16 GB / 24 GB Every token needs the dense 9.9 GB plus the handful of experts the router picks in each layer. The dense part fits in RAM. The experts do not — but you only need a few of them at a time, and the next token often reuses many of the same ones. So the engine treats VRAM, RAM and NVMe as one memory hierarchy: a per-layer LRU cache of recently used experts in RAM, a learned "pinned hot-store" of experts that are used most often, an optional VRAM tier if a GPU is present, and the disk as backing store for everything else. The design choice that makes it a single C file per model rather than a framework: no BLAS, no Python at runtime, no GPU required. The GLM engine started at about 1,300 lines of C. Zero dependencies also means the OS page cache becomes a free second cache layer for expert reads.

The expensive part of streaming is waiting for disk. Colibrì runs a lookahead thread (enabled with PILOT=1) that predicts which experts the next layer will need and starts the reads early. The README's measured figure is that routing decisions are 71.6% predictable one layer ahead, which is enough to hide a large share of the I/O latency behind compute. This is why "tok/s after warmup" is a very different number from "cold tok/s".
documents.s: 1. Router lookahead: routing is 71.6% predictable one layer ahead

documents.t: Put a full copy of the model on a second NVMe and the engine streams from both at once. Each expert hashes deterministically to one drive, weighted by each drive's measured bandwidth, so there is no duplicate caching and the effective read bandwidth is roughly the sum of the two. The DeepSeek V4 Flash benchmark below (RTX 5080 plus two NVMe drives, ~1.6 tok/s) is a dual-drive configuration.
documents.s: 2. Dual-SSD streaming: two drives, one model, summed bandwidth

documents.t: Models with multi-head latent attention (MLA) let Colibrì store a compressed KV state — 576 floats per token instead of 32,768, a 57× reduction. The engine persists that state to a .coli_kv file, so reopening a conversation after a restart does zero re-prefill and is byte-identical to a session that never stopped. On a machine where prefill runs at streaming speed, not re-prefilling a long context is the difference between usable and not.
documents.s: 3. Compressed KV state that survives a restart

documents.t: The project's stated contract: insufficient fast memory only makes it slower; precision and router behavior never silently change. The forward pass is validated token-exact against a transformers oracle. This is the opposite trade from most "fits on a laptop" quantization stories, where you get speed by accepting a different model.
documents.s: 4. Semantics are guaranteed, speed is not

documents.t: Numbers from the project's README (GLM-5.2 unless stated), warm cache where noted: Hardware Tok/s What it means 6× RTX 5090, full expert residency in VRAM 5.8–6.8 (TTFT ~13 s) The ceiling: no disk I/O at all. This is a GPU rig, not "hardware you already own". 128 GB RAM desktop, CPU only, warm cache ~1.8 The realistic best case for a fat workstation without GPUs. Single RTX 5070 Ti (~24 GB VRAM tier) 1.07 A laptop-class GPU roughly doubles the cold-disk floor. RTX 5080 + 32 GB RAM + 2 NVMe, DeepSeek V4 Flash ~1.6 at 3k context, after warmup The dual-SSD path on a smaller model. 25 GB RAM laptop, slow NVMe, cold 0.05–0.1 The headline "744B on 25 GB" configuration. About one token every 10–20 seconds. The variable that decides your number is random-read bandwidth from the drive, not CPU. A cold token needs on the order of 11 GB of expert reads; a PCIe 5.0 NVMe at 13–15 GB/s therefore caps a cold, unprefetched setup near 1 tok/s, and lookahead plus cache hits are what get you above that. Commenters in the launch thread reported cache hit rates around 23% on a 128 GB Apple M5 Max and 0.091 tok/s on an old dual-Xeon with 192 GB of DDR3 — "viable for overnight jobs". So the honest use cases are: overnight or asynchronous batches, private offline experiments with a frontier-class model, research into how MoE inference actually behaves, and warm multi-turn chat on a machine with 100 GB+ of RAM. Interactive pair-programming on a 32 GB laptop is not on the list.

documents.s: Nine model families, and what each one costs in disk

documents.t: MTP heads must be int8. Multi-token-prediction draft heads quantized to int4 give 0–4% draft acceptance — speculative decoding silently does nothing (issue #8). The pre-converted GLM-5.2 container on Hugging Face is int4 for the model and int8 for MTP for exactly this reason. O_DIRECT helps on some drives and hurts on others. Bypassing the page cache measured +34% on NVMe drives with a DRAM cache and bandwidth headroom, and neutral-to-negative on QLC, DRAM-less and virtualized disks. Benchmark both on your drive; do not copy someone else's flag. Speculative decoding is often a net loss on real chat. On multi-turn conversations the MTP and grammar drafters accepted roughly 1–10 of every 24 tokens, and replaying the engine's recurrent attention state for rejected suffixes cost more than the accepted drafts saved. For DeepSeek V4 the project measured 495 seconds of rejected-suffix replay and ships with both drafters off by default (V4_DRAFT=0, V4_MTP=0). Turn them on only if you measure a win. SSD wear is real. Heavy expert reads drive page-cache churn; the README warns about wear on consumer drives, and the launch thread's advice was to disable swap and consider a read-only mount for the model directory. A 370 GB model streamed for hours per day is a workload consumer NVMe was not sold for. One more, less a gotcha than a limitation: the learned expert pinning can overfit to your routing history. It helps repeated workloads; the maintainers say it still needs held-out, cross-session A/B tests before you should trust the gains on new prompts.
documents.s: Four gotchas that cost people days

documents.t: Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Build (checks gcc and OpenMP, compiles, runs self-tests)⌄ git clone https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri && cd colibri/c && ./setup.sh — then make -C c glm for GLM-5.2, or make -C c inkling / make -C c kimi_k3 for the others. Start with OLMoE (7 GB) to prove the build before committing hundreds of gigabytes of downloads. ←PreviousNext→ 2Get the weights in Colibrì's container format⌄ ./coli convert --model /nvme/glm52_i4 downloads and converts shard by shard, one time. For GLM-5.2 a pre-converted int4 container with int8 MTP heads exists on Hugging Face (mastouri/GLM-5.2-colibri-int4-g64-with-int8-mtp). DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Kimi K3 need no conversion: point the engine at the released checkpoint. ←PreviousNext→ 3Check placement before you wait⌄ COLI_MODEL=/nvme/glm52_i4 ./coli plan shows which tensors land in VRAM, RAM and disk for your machine; ./coli doctor runs a readiness check. If plan says most experts will be cold on a slow drive, you now know your tok/s before spending an evening on it. ←PreviousNext→ 4Run: TUI, or API with a dashboard⌄ COLI_MODEL=/nvme/glm52_i4 ./coli chat for a terminal chat. ./coli web --model /nvme/glm52_i4 starts an API server plus a dashboard that shows tier placement, cache hit rate and disk I/O live; ./coli serve is the headless variant. Enable PILOT=1 for router lookahead on any setup that streams from disk. ←PreviousNext→ 5Tune the two knobs that matter, and measure⌄ Try O_DIRECT on and off on your specific drive. Leave speculative decoding off until a benchmark on your own prompts shows it winning. If you have a second NVMe, mirror the model onto it for dual-drive streaming. ←PreviousNext→ A minimal first run on GLM-5.2 (Linux, one NVMe) CopyOpen in Claude↗ git clone https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri && cd colibri/c ./setup.sh make -C c glm ./coli convert --model /nvme/glm52_i4 # one-time download + convert COLI_MODEL=/nvme/glm52_i4 ./coli plan # see what lands where COLI_MODEL=/nvme/glm52_i4 PILOT=1 ./coli chat # first streamed tokens

Path What it is good at Where Colibrì differs llama.cpp / Ollama with GGUF offload (our Ollama guide) Huge model catalog, GPU offload, mature tooling; the GLM-5.2 page covers the 239 GB dynamic 2-bit GGUF route GGUF offload needs the whole quantized model in RAM plus VRAM (256 GB for GLM-5.2 at 2-bit). Colibrì needs 16–24 GB of RAM and a big disk, at the same precision the lab released, not 2-bit. vLLM / SGLang on rented GPUs (Kimi K3 deploy guide) Dozens of tokens per second, batching, multiple users Fast because everything is resident in HBM. Colibrì exists for the case where that hardware is not available or not allowed. Hosted API (DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot) Cheapest per token by far, no hardware The only reason to prefer Colibrì is that the weights and the prompts must never leave the machine, or you want to study MoE inference itself. The right way to think about Colibrì is not "a faster llama.cpp". It is the tool that makes a frontier-sized open model available on a machine that could not otherwise load it, at a speed you schedule around rather than wait on. For a privacy-first stack that mixes a small fast local model for interactive work with a large slow one for batch jobs, see A private local AI stack. 뒤집기용어Expert streaming정의Keep dense weights (attention, embeddings, shared experts) resident; read routed experts from NVMe on demand through a per-layer LRU cache and a learned pinned hot-store. What you'll learn Understand the two-agent split (shopping vs merchant) and why Anthropic did NOT use an intent router or domain subagents Learn the staged-write guardrail: how no model tool call ever moves money or mutates the store — every write ends at a human-approved surface See the three runtime paths (Messages API, Agent SDK, Managed Agents) and how the SAME core code plugs into all three Steal three transferable patterns for any agent that touches a real business system: server-issued IDs, fenced third-party text, and prompt-vs-skill split On September 2, 2026 Anthropic published anthropics/commerce-agents — an Apache 2.0 reference blueprint for building shopping and merchant agents on Claude. It ships two working agents, four vertical examples (retail, travel, telecom, entertainment), and — crucially — a set of guardrail patterns implemented in code, not in prompts. Anthropic states the repo is a reference implementation they will not maintain as a product and does not accept outside contributions. The interesting thing is not that you can now build a shopping bot. The interesting thing is the shape: an unusually opinionated take on how an agent that touches real business systems should be structured. Everything below is transferable to any agent that has to write to a real backend — inventory, customer records, banking, ops tooling.

Anthropic ships one shopping agent (customer-facing) and one merchant agent (staff-facing), each with its own backend interface (StorefrontBackend and MerchantBackend) and its own set of skills. They deliberately did not build: an intent router that dispatches to sub-agents per-domain subagents (a "cart agent" + "returns agent" + "search agent") one monolithic agent that does both consumer and staff work Instead: one unified agent per audience, in a standard agent loop, with skills and tools. Their guidance in the anatomy of effective commerce agents post: "anything the agent needs on most turns generally goes in the system prompt" — so for a shopping agent, catalog search lives in the prompt because it's on nearly every turn. "The rest goes in skills." Customer care, personalization, returns — skills. This is a strong opinion. Intent routers and domain subagents are the default architecture in a lot of tutorials, and Anthropic is telling you: for a single audience with tightly coupled sessions, don't.
documents.s: The split: two agents, not one

documents.t: Pro tip The single most important line in the blueprint: 'No model tool call moves money or changes the business.' Every mutation goes through a server-controlled approval step. If you take one thing from the repo, take this. The blueprint enforces safety in code, not prompts. The mechanism has three parts: Guided walkthrough1 of 3 11. Server issues every ID the model is allowed to reference⌄ The server maintains a per-session record of every product ID, SKU, campaign ID, and price ID it has handed the model. Writes and renders will ONLY accept IDs from that record. If the model hallucinates a SKU, the harness refuses — no prompt engineering required. ←PreviousNext→ 22. Every write is staged, never applied⌄ Order placement, payments, refunds, price changes, and campaign launches all end in a server-generated draft with its own approval ID. The tool call returns the draft ID and a preview. Nothing is live yet. ←PreviousNext→ 33. Approval happens on a real human surface⌄ A staged change only succeeds when the approval ID is signed off through a real UI — a button in the operator's portal, a confirmation in the CLI. The agent cannot self-approve; the approval endpoint doesn't accept model-generated identity. ←PreviousNext→ The blueprint also handles two other classic footguns: Regulated content: for fees, disclosures, and price-shown-to-consumer, the model chooses which product to disclose; the words come from server-supplied approved copy. The model never writes disclosure text. Third-party text sanitization: any user-generated content (reviews, seller notes, messages) is wrapped in "fenced text" markers before it reaches the model, so it can't smuggle instructions into the prompt.

The blueprint places no orders and charges no cards. Checkout is rendered for the host application to complete. In Anthropic's words, this "keeps payment handling, fraud rules and credentials outside the agent." Visa, Mastercard, and Accenture are named partners on the announcement, but the payment step lives in your existing checkout or an agentic payments provider — never in the model's tool surface. This is another opinionated line: if it can lose money in one shot, the model doesn't touch it.

The repo splits every agent into a core package (types, backend interface, prompt, tool contracts) and separate runtime packages that adapt the core to different serving surfaces: Messages API — the reference loop CopyOpen in Claude↗ from shopping_agent import ShoppingAgentConfig from shopping_agent_runtime import ShoppingAgent agent = ShoppingAgent( backend=your_backend, skills_dir=Path("shopping-agent/skills"), config=ShoppingAgentConfig(brand_name="Your Store"), ) async for event in agent.stream_turn(messages, session, state): # yields: text_delta | tool_call | ui | cart_update | turn_complete ... await agent.update_memory(messages, session) Agent SDK — with a local console CopyOpen in Claude↗ python shopping-agent/runtime-agent-sdk/main.py \ --once "a two-person tent under $250" python merchant-agent/runtime-agent-sdk/main.py # prints staged changes and waits for y/n approval Managed Agents (beta) — hosted CopyOpen in Claude↗ scripts/deploy_managed_agent.sh \ shopping-agent/managed-agents/shopping-agent # The manifest declares tools + a storefront MCP server; # Anthropic hosts the loop. The same core/ code runs under all three, which is the actual portable pattern: keep the agent's contract (tools, prompt, backend interface) separate from the serving harness. If you swap Messages API for Managed Agents six months from now, only the runtime package changes.

Long-term memory (preferences, past orders, service notes) is persisted in your existing databases, not in model context. Extraction happens asynchronously after the conversation ends — you don't pay latency to update memory on the hot path. On the next turn, the runtime hydrates relevant memory into the system prompt. This is worth internalizing even if you're not building commerce: shoving conversation summaries into context on every turn is a common performance mistake. The blueprint's shape — write async, read on turn-start — is the cheaper one.

examples/ includes end-to-end demos for four verticals, each with a different structural wrinkle you can copy: Retail — the base case. Standard catalog, cart, checkout. Travel — date-bound inventory (a flight seat expires), itinerary presentation with multi-leg comparison. Telecom — account context ("your current plan is X"), plan matrices, regulated fee disclosure. Entertainment — timed holds on tickets, waitlists, venue seat maps. If your product isn't commerce but has any of these traits (expiring inventory, regulated disclosure, timed holds), the matching vertical is worth reading before you design your own agent.
documents.s: The four verticals (and why they differ)

고급 모든 주요 랩이 이제 화면을 보고 클릭할 수 있는 모델을 내놓습니다. Anthropic의 computer use 도구, OpenAI의 computer 도구, Google의 computer_use 도구는 모두 같은 형태의 문제를 풉니다 — 스크린샷을 찍고, 액션을 정하고, 실행하고, 다시 스크린샷 — 그리고 셋 모두 클릭이 40픽셀씩 빗나가기 시작하기 전까지는 눈에 띄지 않는 방식으로 서로 와이어 호환이 되지 않습니다. 이 페이지는 리더보드가 아니라 하네스 수준의 가이드입니다. 리더보드는 매달 바뀌지만, 아래의 실패 모드는 첫 프리뷰가 나온 이래 그대로입니다. What you'll learn 세 제공자가 공유하는 에이전트 루프 — 그리고 그들이 갈라지는 세 지점 이해하기 첫 시도 대부분을 조용히 망가뜨리는 좌표 버그 고치기 (Retina, 다운스케일링, 이미지 크기 제한) 각 제공자의 안전 게이트 알기 — 그것은 선택적 부가물이 아니라 프로토콜의 일부입니다 OSWorld를 정직하게 읽기: 인간 기준선이 실제로 뜻하는 것 추론 노력(effort)을 올바르게 고르기 — 가장 싼 설정은 여러분이 짐작하는 그것이 아닙니다 최종 검증: 2026-07-14. 이 분야의 모델 이름, 베타 헤더, 픽셀 제한, 벤치마크 점수는 빠르게 움직이고, 모든 제공자가 여전히 자사 computer-use 표면을 프리뷰 또는 베타로 표시합니다. 아래의 메커니즘은 오래갑니다. 출시 전에 특정 숫자, 헤더, 모델 ID는 출처에 링크된 제공자 문서에서 다시 확인하세요. 다음에서 확인하세요: 공식 출처.

브랜딩을 걷어내면 셋 다 같은 상태 기계입니다. Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1작업과 스크린샷을 보낸다⌄ 모델은 여러분의 지시와 현재 화면의 이미지를 받습니다. 일부 제공자는 현재 URL이나 최근 액션의 짧은 이력도 원합니다. ←PreviousNext→ 2모델은 결과가 아니라 액션을 반환한다⌄ (x, y)를 클릭하라. 이것을 입력하라. 여기를 스크롤하라. 여러분의 코드가 무언가를 하라는 요청입니다 — 모델 자신은 머신을 건드릴 수 없습니다. ←PreviousNext→ 3여러분의 하네스가 그것을 실행한다⌄ 이건 여러분의 몫입니다. Anthropic은 명확히 말합니다: 애플리케이션이 도구를 실행해야 하며, Claude가 직접 실행할 수 없습니다. 스크린샷 캡처, 마우스, 키보드는 여러분이 구현합니다. ←PreviousNext→ 4다시 스크린샷을 찍어 되먹인다⌄ 새 화면이 도구 결과로 돌아갑니다. 모델은 자기 액션의 결과를 봅니다 — 이것이 피드백 신호의 전부입니다. ←PreviousNext→ 5액션이 더 오지 않을 때까지 반복한다⌄ 종료는 'done' 플래그가 아니라 추가 액션 요청의 부재입니다. 루프에는 자체 스텝 상한과 정체 감지가 필요합니다. ←PreviousNext→ 사람들이 놓치는 귀결: 세상에 대한 모델의 유일한 지각은 여러분이 보낸 이미지입니다. 아래의 모든 실패는 사실 그 이미지의 실패이거나, 그것이 함의하는 좌표 공간의 실패입니다.

갈라짐은 "누가 더 똑똑한가"가 아닙니다. 계약입니다. Anthropic (Claude) OpenAI (GPT) Google (Gemini) 액션 공간 원시 데스크톱 프리미티브: screenshot, left_click, type, key, scroll, drag, hold_key, wait, 그리고 최신 도구 버전의 zoom 구조화된 UI 액션: click, double_click, scroll, type, keypress, drag, move, wait, screenshot 의미론적 액션: click/type뿐 아니라 navigate, go_back, go_forward, open_app, long_press — 브라우저와 모바일 개념이 일급 시민 좌표 픽셀 크기를 보내면 모델이 그 공간의 원시 픽셀 좌표를 반환 같은 픽셀 계약, 권장 데스크톱 크기 제공 동일. 각 액션의 이유를 설명하는 intent 필드 추가 루프 배관 이미지를 담은 도구 결과 블록 computer_call → call_id로 연결된 computer_call_output. previous_response_id가 이력을 실어 나르므로 재전송 불필요 함수 호출 → 새 스크린샷과 함께 function_result 안전 게이트 스크린샷에 인젝션 분류기가 자동 실행 명시적으로 확인해야 하는 pending_safety_checks 정책 범주가 붙은 safety_decision 강점 영역 범용 데스크톱 / OS 수준 제어 데스크톱과 브라우저, 그리고 코드 실행 경로 브라우저 우선. 모바일에 강함. 데스크톱 OS 제어에는 명시적으로 최적화되지 않음 마지막의 Anthropic/Google 행이 아키텍처를 결정합니다. Google의 액션 공간은 의미론적입니다 — go_back은 모델이 이름 부를 수 있는 개념입니다. Anthropic의 것은 기계적입니다 — 뒤로 가려면 모델이 뒤로 가기 버튼을 찾아 클릭하거나 올바른 키 조합을 눌러야 합니다. 의미론적 액션은 브라우저 안에서 더 믿을 만하고 바깥에서는 쓸모없습니다. 기계적 프리미티브는 어디서나 동작하고 더 자주 실패합니다. 그러니 computer-use 에이전트를 제공자 간에 이식하는 것은 모델 교체가 아닙니다. 하네스의 액션 실행기를 다시 쓰는 일입니다. 그에 맞게 예산을 잡으세요. (코딩 에이전트 CLI 비교와 같은 교훈: 여러분이 실제로 결혼한 상대는 모델이 아니라 하네스입니다.)
이 페이지에서 가장 값어치 있는 항목입니다. 거의 모두가 부딪히고, 증상이 "모델이 클릭을 못 한다"처럼 보이기 때문입니다. 클릭을 못 하는 게 아닙니다. 여러분의 이미지와 좌표 공간이 서로 어긋난 것입니다. 독립적인 세 가지 원인이 있고, 겹칩니다.

macOS Retina 디스플레이는 디바이스 픽셀 비율 2로 스크린샷을 캡처합니다 — 이미지가 논리적 화면 좌표의 두 배 해상도입니다. 그것을 그대로 보내면 모델은 2880 너비 이미지 위에서 추론하는데 여러분의 클릭 실행기는 1440 너비 논리 포인트로 생각합니다. 모든 클릭이 의도한 위치의 대략 절반 지점에, 일관되게, 한 방향으로 떨어집니다. 해법: 보내기 전에 2로 다운스케일하거나, 또는 모델이 반환한 좌표를 절반으로 나누세요. 둘 다 하지는 마세요.
documents.s: 1. Retina / HiDPI가 이미지를 두 배로 만든다

documents.t: 모델에는 이미지 크기 제한이 있고 — 같은 랩의 모델들 사이에서도 다릅니다. Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7은 긴 변 기준 2576 픽셀까지 받습니다. 이전 Claude 모델들은 1568 픽셀과 총 약 1.15 메가픽셀까지 받습니다. 여기에 함정이 있습니다. 더 큰 것을 보내면 API가 에러를 내는 대신 알아서 다운스케일합니다. 그러면 모델은 자신이 본 이미지의 공간에서 좌표를 반환하는데, 리사이즈가 서버 측에서 일어났으므로 여러분은 스케일 팩터를 결코 알지 못합니다. 정말로 거대한 이미지(한 변이 약 8,000 px 초과)만 검증 에러로 곧바로 거부됩니다. 그러니 "친절한" 동작이 곧 버그입니다. 항상 클라이언트 측에서 리사이즈하고, display_width_px/display_height_px를 실제로 보낸 크기로 설정하고, 반환된 좌표를 직접 되돌려 스케일하세요.

OpenAI 도구에서는 스크린샷에 detail: "original"을 써야 합니다 — 이 작업에 한해서는 "high"와 "low" 둘 다 클릭 정확도를 떨어뜨립니다. 그리고 종횡비를 보존하지 않고 리사이즈하면 클릭이 맞는 영역에 떨어지고 대상은 빗나갑니다. 좌표 스케일링 — 해법의 형태 CopyOpen in Claude↗ # Before sending: shrink to fit the model's image limit, remember the factor. LONG_EDGE_LIMIT = 2576 # check YOUR model's limit; older Claude models: 1568 scale = min(1.0, LONG_EDGE_LIMIT / max(width, height)) sent_w, sent_h = round(width * scale), round(height * scale) # -> send the resized image, and declare display_width_px=sent_w, display_height_px=sent_h # After the model replies: map its coordinates back to the real screen. real_x, real_y = model_x / scale, model_y / scale # On a Retina capture you did NOT pre-downscale, divide by the device pixel ratio too.

증상 거의 확실히 클릭이 한 방향으로 일관되게 어긋남 선언한 display_width_px/display_height_px가 실제로 보낸 이미지와 맞지 않음 클릭이 맞는 영역에 떨어지지만 작은 대상은 빗나감 다운스케일로 디테일 손실, 또는 리사이즈에서 종횡비 왜곡 어디서나 정확도가 나쁨 해상도가 너무 낮음 — 1280x720을 하한으로 시도해 보세요 모델이 작은 텍스트(탭 제목, 파일명, 줄 번호)를 잘못 읽음 확대가 필요한데 활성화하지 않음 벤더 자신들이 제시한 해상도 가이드: Anthropic은 일반 데스크톱에 1024x768 또는 1280x720을, 웹 앱에 1280x800 또는 1366x768을 권하며 1920x1080을 넘기지 말라고 명시합니다. OpenAI는 1440x900 또는 1600x900을 권합니다. 크다고 더 좋은 게 아닙니다 — 픽셀에 토큰을 지불하고는 다운스케일에서 그 디테일을 버리게 됩니다.

Claude의 최신 computer 도구 버전(computer_20251124)은 zoom 액션을 추가하는데, 기본은 꺼짐입니다 — enable_zoom: true를 설정해야 합니다. 켜면 Claude는 스크린샷의 기본 해상도에서 읽기 힘든 작은 텍스트가 필요할 때 영역을 확대합니다. 사이드바 파일명, 탭 제목, 상태 표시줄 텍스트, 줄 번호, 버튼 레이블 같은 것들입니다. 눈에 잘 안 띄는 운영 노트: Claude가 기대하는 때에 확대를 하지 않고 있다면, 해법은 대개 화면 전체가 아니라 특정 영역이나 요소에 대해 묻는 것입니다.

이것을 덧붙이는 물건으로 여기지 마세요. 세 API 모두에서 안전 메커니즘이 루프의 형태를 바꿉니다. Anthropic은 모델이 프롬프트 인젝션에 저항하도록 훈련했고 동시에 computer-use 도구가 쓰이면 여러분의 프롬프트에 분류기를 자동으로 돌립니다. 분류기가 스크린샷 안에서 인젝션으로 보이는 것을 포착하면, 다음 액션 전에 사용자에게 확인을 구하도록 모델을 유도합니다. 사람이 있을 때는 훌륭하고 무인 파이프라인에는 명백히 틀린 동작입니다 — 그래서 지원팀 문의로 열리는 옵트아웃이 있습니다. OpenAI는 루프가 진행되기 전에 여러분의 코드가 명시적으로 확인해야 하는(acknowledged_safety_checks) pending_safety_checks를 노출합니다. 게이트가 여러분 손에 있고, 건너뛰는 것은 코드에서 내리는 결정입니다. Google은 safety_decision을 반환합니다 — allowed, require_confirmation, blocked — 그리고 FINANCIAL_TRANSACTIONS, COMMUNICATION_TOOL, ACCOUNT_CREATION, SENSITIVE_DATA_MODIFICATION, LEGAL_TERMS_AND_AGREEMENTS를 포함한 정책 범주가 이를 구동합니다. 스크린샷의 프롬프트 인젝션 스크리닝은 옵트인으로 제공됩니다. 위협은 실재하고 구체적입니다. 스크린샷은 신뢰할 수 없는 입력입니다. 웹페이지에, 이미지에, 에이전트가 연 PDF에 렌더링된 텍스트 — 그 전부가 여러분의 지시와 같은 채널로 모델에 도달합니다. Anthropic 자신의 문서는 Claude가 어떤 상황에서는 여러분의 지시와 충돌하더라도 콘텐츠에서 발견한 지시를 따를 것이라고 지적합니다. 모든 제공자의 완화책은 같은 세 규칙으로 수렴합니다: 환경을 격리하고, 영향이 큰 액션에는 사람을 두고, 화면 위의 모든 것을 적대적이라고 취급하라. 에이전트가 로그인해야 한다면 그 위험은 급격히 올라갑니다 — 자격 증명 더하기 주입 가능한 콘텐츠는 이 분야 최악의 조합입니다. 방어 플레이북은 로컬 및 하이브리드 에이전트 보안과 프롬프트 인젝션을 보세요.

OSWorld는 공유 잣대이고, 속이기 어렵기 때문에 좋은 잣대입니다. 에이전트를 실제 애플리케이션이 있는 실제 OS에 떨어뜨리고 실행 기반 검증으로 채점합니다 — 에이전트가 그렇게 주장했는지가 아니라 파일이 실제로 저장되었는지 스크립트가 확인합니다. 벤치마크는 369개 작업에 걸쳐 있고(표준 평가 세트에서는 361개, 일부 Google Drive 작업은 수동 설정이 필요하므로) 134개의 실행 기반 평가 함수를 제공합니다. OSWorld-Verified는 커뮤니티가 보고한 깨진 예제를 고치고 평가 시간을 AWS에서 약 한 시간으로 줄인 정제판입니다. 함께 붙들 가치가 있는 두 숫자. 인간 기준선은 약 72.4%입니다. 100%가 아닙니다. 이 작업들은 정말로 까다롭고 사람도 헤맵니다. OSWorld가 출시됐을 때 최고 모델은 12.24%를 기록했습니다. 프런티어 에이전트들은 이제 70%대 이상을 보고합니다 — 즉 "에이전트가 컴퓨터 사용에서 인간 수준에 도달했다"는 헤드라인은 산술적으로는 방어 가능하지만 실무적으로는 오도합니다. 벤치마크 점수는 코딩 벤치마크와 똑같이 모델 + 하네스 + 스캐폴드 결과입니다(능력–신뢰성 격차 참고). 여러분의 하네스는 그들의 하네스가 아닙니다. 그리고 단일 작업 75% 성공률은 잔혹하게 복리로 줄어듭니다. 각 단계가 95% 신뢰성인 여덟 단계 워크플로는 약 66%만 성공합니다. OSWorld는 능력이 존재한다는 증거로 다루고, 여러분의 제품이 동작한다는 유일한 증거는 자체 평가 세트로 삼으세요.

Claude computer use에 한해, Anthropic의 내부 벤치마킹은 통상적인 직관을 뒤집는 가이드를 줍니다. Opus 4.7: 기본은 high 노력. 처리량이 많거나 비용에 민감한 워크로드에서는 low로 내리세요. Sonnet 4.6과 Opus 4.6: medium이 정확도 대비 비용 비율이 가장 좋습니다. max는 피하세요 — UI 작업에서는 정확도 향상 없이 토큰 비용만 더합니다. 반직관적인 것: 그 모델들에서 low 노력은 사고를 아예 끄는 것보다 출력 토큰을 더 적게 씁니다. 약간의 사고가 실수를 막고, 실수는 재시도를 부르고, 재시도는 사고보다 훨씬 많은 토큰을 씁니다. 그러니 "돈 아끼려 사고를 끄자"는 computer use에서는 흔히 틀립니다. 가장 싼 것은 약간의 사고입니다. 모델 선택의 또 다른 주름: 기계적 클릭 정밀도는 지능과 같은 축이 아닙니다. Sonnet 4.6은 클릭에서 Opus 4.6보다 기계적으로 더 정밀하고, 스크린샷이 심하게 다운스케일됐을 때 더 견고합니다. Opus 4.7은 그 격차를 좁히고 픽셀 제한을 올려서 애초에 다운스케일이 덜 필요합니다. 뒤집기용어Mac에서 클릭이 왜 의도한 위치의 절반에 떨어지나?정의Retina는 디바이스 픽셀 비율 2로 캡처합니다 — 스크린샷이 논리 좌표 공간의 2배입니다. 이미지를 2로 다운스케일하거나, 반환된 좌표를 절반으로 나누세요. 둘 다는 아닙니다.Enter 또는 스페이스 키를 눌러 카드를 뒤집습니다. 좌우 화살표 키로 카드를 이동할 수 있습니다.용어가 표시되었습니다. ←이전 1 / 7 다음→

documents.t: Guided walkthrough1 of 6 1언제나 샌드박스 먼저⌄ 가치 있는 것이 하나도 없는 컨테이너나 VM. 모든 제공자가 이렇게 말하고 진심입니다: 에이전트는 언젠가 여러분이 의도하지 않은 것을 클릭합니다. ←PreviousNext→ 2좌표 공간을 고정하라⌄ 캡처하고, 모델 제한에 맞춰 클라이언트 측에서 리사이즈하고, 실제로 보낸 크기를 정확히 선언하고, 스케일 팩터를 보관하세요. 한 번 짜 두고 다시는 생각하지 마세요. ←PreviousNext→ 3루프에 상한을 두라⌄ 종료는 '더 이상 액션이 반환되지 않음'인데 — 에이전트가 닫지 못하는 모달에 갇히면 그것은 절대 발동하지 않습니다. 최대 스텝 예산과 정체 감지(N회 연속 동일 스크린샷)를 추가하세요. ←PreviousNext→ 4안전 게이트 정책을 명시적으로 정하라⌄ 사람이 개입하거나, 아니면 옵트아웃과 좁은 폭발 반경으로 무인 운영하거나. 확인 프롬프트가 cron 작업을 교착시킬 때 우연히 알게 되지 마세요. ←PreviousNext→ 5두 번째 기능을 만들기 전에 열 개짜리 평가 세트를 만들라⌄ OSWorld처럼 실행 검증으로: 에이전트가 그랬다고 말한 게 아니라 세상이 바뀌었는지 확인하세요. 여러분 시스템에 대해 의미 있는 유일한 숫자입니다. ←PreviousNext→ 6가능하면 픽셀보다 API를 선호하라⌄ 가장 믿을 만한 computer-use 에이전트는 컴퓨터를 쓸 필요가 없는 에이전트입니다. 대상에 API나 MCP 서버나 CLI가 있다면 그 경로가 더 빠르고 싸고 신뢰성이 몇 자릿수 높습니다. 화면은 목표가 아니라 폴백입니다. ←PreviousNext→ 마지막 단계가 전략적인 것입니다. Computer use는 API가 없는 소프트웨어를 위한 만능 어댑터입니다 — 레거시 데스크톱 앱, 벤더 포털, 통합 스토리 없이 로그인 뒤에 있는 모든 것. 훌륭한 해킹이고, 여전히 해킹입니다. 먼저 MCP와 진짜 도구에 손을 뻗으세요. 고급 DeepSeek Harness — the command is dsh — is DeepSeek's open-source agent harness. It appeared on GitHub on 13 August 2026, carries 242,626 stars and 29,081 forks as of today, is MIT licensed and written in TypeScript. On 1 October 2026 DeepSeek added signed desktop installers, which is what put it back on the Hacker News front page. Its one-line pitch is the repository description: "Everything is a Plugin." That phrase is on the README of roughly every agent framework ever published, and it almost always means "we have a plugin folder." Here it means something much stronger and much weirder, stated plainly in docs/architecture.md: the model adapter, the tool registry, the session log and the agent loop itself are plugins, "so each is replaceable from configuration." You can delete the agent loop from a YAML file and drop in your own without forking anything. That design has consequences — some excellent, some expensive. This page is about the ones you cannot read off the landing page. What you'll learn Understand what 'everything is a plugin' buys you here, and what Cordis — the framework underneath — actually guarantees Run your existing Claude Code hooks.json inside dsh, and know which subset survives the bridge Point dsh at Claude, GPT or a company gateway, and know why an OAuth subscription will not work Use PTC mode (run_code) deliberately instead of accidentally Read the three sandbox modes against the kernel primitive each one really uses Avoid the five configuration traps that cost an hour each 최종 검증: 2026-10-03. Star counts, the npm version and the desktop installer matrix are perishable. The npm latest tag currently resolves to 0.2.0-rc.2 — a release candidate, not a stable release — and SAFETY.md describes the project as "experimental developer-preview software" that "has not undergone a security audit." The README warns of compatibility-breaking changes. Treat every file path, service key and config field below as true for the 0.2 line and re-check against the repository docs before you build on them. The architecture and safety claims here come from the repository's own documentation, not from secondary coverage. 다음에서 확인하세요: 공식 출처.
documents.s: DeepSeek Harness: the agent where the agent loop itself is a plugin

documents.t: Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Start it⌄ `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` boots the web profile, prints a URL — `http://127.0.0.1:3080` — and opens your browser. No clone, no build. The directory you invoke it from becomes the default workspace root, but a fresh Web UI has no workspace selected until you add one, and the composer stays disabled until you do. ←PreviousNext→ 2Give it a model⌄ Settings → Models. The DeepSeek card takes an API key from platform.deepseek.com. Add a third-party provider and the shipped catalog offers provider ids including `anthropic`, `openai`, `moonshotai` (Kimi) and `zai` (GLM). Model changes apply on the next request — no restart. ←PreviousNext→ 3Understand where it put things⌄ Keys land in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`, write-only: the settings page gets a redacted descriptor back, never the secret, and your settings store only a credential reference. Everything else you change in the UI is written to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` — the same file you can hand-edit. ←PreviousNext→ 4Pick an entry mode⌄ `dsh web` is one of five shipped profiles. `dsh --profile headless "run the tests"` runs one persisted session, prints the final answer and exits — that is your CI entry point. `dsh --profile acp` serves automation clients over ACP stdio. `dsh --profile sdk` serves SDK clients over JSON-RPC stdio. The `desktop` name is reserved for the Electron app's own profile and the npm CLI refuses to boot it. ←PreviousNext→ 5Install plugins like npm packages⌄ `dsh plugin --profile web <pnpm args>` forwards straight to pnpm inside the profile directory. Plugins are ordinary packages in the profile's own `node_modules`. Community plugins are discoverable by the `dsh-plugin` GitHub topic. ←PreviousNext→

Underneath dsh is Cordis, a plugin framework vendored into the repository (vendor/) and described in an arXiv paper the project cites — A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability, arXiv:2608.25512, submitted 26 August 2026, from authors at Peking University and DeepSeek-AI. The paper's two ideas map directly onto how the harness behaves at runtime: Temporal composability — a component's side effects can be completely reversed when it is removed. In the harness this is ctx.effect(): prompt sections, tool schemas, model adapters, providers and listeners are all installed as reversible effects, so unloading a plugin unwinds its registrations in order rather than leaving orphans behind. Spatial composability — dependencies resolve reactively. A plugin names the services it needs via inject, and Cordis simply does not start it until those services exist. There is no boot sequence to maintain; load order is a consequence of declared requirements. A service claims a stable key on the shared context. The names are the architecture: Service key What owns it ctx.llm the LLM adapter registry — the model seam ctx.tools the tool registry and its scoped execution pipeline ctx.agentLoop the default agent-loop driver ctx.agents the live agent registry ctx.sessions the append-only SessionEvent log ctx.systemPrompt system-prompt assembly ctx.fs filesystem access ctx.subprocess subprocess execution ctx.sandbox subprocess confinement ctx.subagents subagent delegation ctx.ptcRuntime program execution for run_code ctx.credentials the credential seam The repository calls these capability seams, and splits every one into three roles: the package that declares the service, the packages that implement it, and the packages that consume it. ctx.sandbox is declared by packages/sandbox/sandbox, implemented by sandbox-local and sandbox-windows-acl, consumed by tool-bash and the PTC runtime. Replace the implementation and every consumer follows, with no consumer edits. Communication between plugins is typed events with five declared dispatch modes, and the mode is part of an event's public contract: Mode Awaited Order Returns a value emit no registration order no waterfall no registration order yes parallel yes all at once no serial yes registration order yes bail no registration order, stops at first bail yes waterfall is the interesting one: it is around-middleware. A listener gets (...args, next), calls next() to pass a possibly-wrapped result down the chain, or returns without calling next() to short-circuit. For single-decision events — "may this tool run?" — short-circuiting is the design: a policy listener that owns the decision returns without delegating, while a listener that merely annotates must delegate. If you have written a Claude Code hook that returns a deny decision, you already know this shape; the difference is that here it is the native extension mechanism rather than a shell-out. The agent loop runs turns (zero or more steps) and steps (one model request plus its tool calls), and the published extension sequence is agent/pre-step → agent/request → llm/stream → tools/* → step/end. Those are the hook points. You do not patch the loop; you listen to it.
documents.s: "Everything is a plugin" is a load-bearing claim

documents.t: This is the single most under-reported fact about dsh. packages/hooks ships three packages: hook-protocol (the shared engine), hooks-claude-code and hooks-codex. Point the Claude Code bridge at an existing hooks.json and your hooks run inside dsh when sessions start, prompts arrive, tools run and runs stop. The group README is explicit about what they can do: block prompts or tool calls with model-visible messages, add conversation context, or require the run to continue. The limit is equally explicit, and it is the thing to check before you plan a migration: each integration supports only the command-hook subset documented by its source tool. So your command-type hooks port. Anything that depends on Claude Code behaviour outside that subset does not. If you have a hooks layer you trust — see Claude Code hooks — this is a genuine "bring your guardrails with you" path, not a rewrite.
documents.s: 1. It will run your existing Claude Code hooks.json

documents.t: The provider list shipped in the installed catalog includes anthropic and openai by name. For anything not in the catalog — a relay, a company gateway, a self-hosted server — the custom-provider form asks for a Provider ID, a base URL, a credential and an API protocol, and offers exactly three: OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages. In cordis.patch.yml these are stored as openai-completions, openai-responses and anthropic-messages. Two consequences people trip over: A provider speaks one protocol. A gateway that serves both OpenAI and Anthropic shapes needs two provider entries, not one. OAuth sign-in is not supported. The providers guide states it directly, using Codex as its example: providers that sign in with OAuth "are not supported here yet." That means API-key billing, not a seat you already pay for. If you were hoping to drive dsh off an existing assistant subscription, budget for metered tokens instead — the arithmetic is in what AI costs across providers. There is also a model-discovery button that asks your endpoint which models it serves. Useful, with a caveat worth internalising: a built-in provider is always answered from the installed catalog even when its base URL points at a gateway. So if you want to see what a gateway really serves, you have to add it as a custom provider. Otherwise you are reading DeepSeek's shipped list back to yourself.
documents.s: 2. You can point it at Claude — but not with your subscription

documents.t: packages/ptc-runtime is the capability family behind what the tool registry presents to the model as run_code. The contract: the model writes one program that calls host-provided functions as ordinary async calls, and only the program's printed output and return value come back. Not the intermediate tool results. Not twenty round-trips. The specifics: The TypeScript backend runs each program in a fresh managed Node process under the resolved sandbox policy. Each run starts with no state from earlier programs. There is no implicit REPL session to lean on; carry state through files or the return value. Failures come back as results, not exceptions, so a caller can diagnose them or hand them to the model. An experimental Python backend exists, owning an fd-3 wire protocol between the Node host and a CPython subprocess, for when you genuinely need CPython. If this pattern is new to you, the clearest write-up of why it saves so much context is on Pi 1.0 and the codemode trick: tool results that never enter the transcript cannot inflate it. The same logic applies here. The difference is that in dsh the program runtime is a swappable seam (ctx.ptcRuntime) rather than a fixed sandbox choice.
documents.s: 3. run_code is codemode, and it is a first-class runtime

documents.t: The three modes will look familiar if you have configured Codex: Mode What a subprocess may do to files read-only read only workspace-write write only under the session workspace danger-full-access unrestricted What is more interesting is the backend table, because it tells you what is really enforcing the policy on your machine: Linux — bwrap, then Landlock as the fallback rung. macOS — Seatbelt. Windows — a restricted token, with sandbox-windows-acl as the write-restriction backend: confined children may write only in the workspace and a private temp directory. A denied call can retry through a user-approved one-time escalation, so the policy is a prompt-and-proceed boundary rather than a hard wall. And then the caveat, which the package README states itself and which you should quote to anyone who tells you this is "sandboxed": confinement is same-world only. It shares the host kernel and the host filesystem. Real isolation — containers, microVMs, remote executors — does not register here at all; it replaces whole capabilities instead. SAFETY.md is unusually candid for a 242k-star repository, and worth reading before a first run rather than after. It says the harness can execute model-generated code, load third-party plugins, reach the network and touch processes, credentials and files; that there is no inherent guarantee that sandboxing, approval prompts and permission controls will prevent damage to anything reachable; and that the software "must not be treated as secure or production-ready." Its own recommendations are the boring correct ones: disposable VMs or containers, backups of anything inside the project scope, and no sensitive credentials unless you accept the risk. The same reasoning applies to any harness you run locally — see securing local and hybrid agents and sandboxing and credential masking. There is also a small guard group worth knowing about: timeout-policy and repeat-tool-reminder — the latter being a nudge for the failure mode where a model calls the same tool in a loop.
documents.s: The sandbox: three modes, three kernel primitives, one honest caveat

documents.t: dsh persists sessions as a versioned JSONL file — session.vN.jsonl[.zstd] — with migration chains between versions, through a ctx.sessionPersistence seam whose shipped implementation is session-persistence-jsonl. Committed events include turn/start, step/start, user/message, assistant/message, tool/result and turn/end. The invariant behind it is the part to steal even if you never run dsh: "model-visible means logged." Every input the model saw must be reconstructable from the log. Live events exist separately, for driving UI in real time; they are explicitly not the record of truth. That single rule is what makes the surrounding packages possible: session-query-sqlite — query sessions out of SQLite instead of grepping JSONL. dsh-session-projection with ctx.sessionProjections — fold session state incrementally rather than replaying from zero. llm-replay plus token-meter ("replay token measurement") — replay a recorded session and measure its token cost, which is how you compare two prompt or model changes on identical inputs instead of on vibes. compaction-tool-result-pruner — described as model-free tool-result pruning, i.e. shrinking the transcript without paying a model to summarise it. Compare with Claude's own approach in context compaction. If you have ever tried to debug an agent run and discovered your logs recorded the rendered UI rather than the bytes the model received, you already know why this invariant is worth more than most features.
documents.s: The session log is the product

documents.t: dsh speaks MCP over both stdio and Streamable HTTP, using the official SDK for negotiation, discovery, validation and cancellation. The design choices are unusual enough to list: Servers are opt-in, one plugin entry per server. You configure one @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client entry per server in the Cordis scope you want it visible in. There is deliberately no shared ctx.mcp service: the client is a connection plugin and a consumer of the tool registry. No configured server means no MCP tax. A caller with no visible configured server receives no MCP prompt text and no MCP tools, in native or PTC mode. Zero bytes, not "a small section." That matters more than it sounds — see the real cost of MCP tools. Public tool names include the server name, so identically-named tools from two servers stay distinct. A serverName must be unique inside its registration scope, but separate agent scopes may reuse it. Server instructions join the logged system prompt, bounded by the client's maxInstructionBytes. A verbose server cannot quietly annex your prompt — but note that this is also the channel through which a malicious server speaks to your model. That is the attack surface described in MCP tool poisoning and rug pulls. A failed tool-list refresh retains the previous tool generation rather than dropping your tools mid-session, and there is no product setting that forces a protocol revision — negotiation follows the SDK's supported revisions.
documents.s: MCP here is a per-server plugin, not a global registry

documents.t: A profile directory holds a package.json — out-of-tree plugin dependencies plus a dsh.profile manifest with an ordered bundles list — and a cordis.patch.yml, your own patch layer. The composed tree is built over an empty root in this order: Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Each bundle's patch, in `dsh.profile.bundles` order⌄ Bundles resolve from the dsh installation first — `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`, `dsh-web-app`, `dsh-headless`, `dsh-sdk-app`, `dsh-sdk-minimal`, `dsh-acp-app` — then from the profile's own `node_modules`, where pnpm installs out-of-tree plugins. `dsh-base` is the shared floor: model adapters, tools, persistence, sandbox policy. A bundle declares itself through a `dsh` field in its `package.json`. ←PreviousNext→ 2Then the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`⌄ `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`. For a plain `dsh web` launch the profile is `web`. This is the file the Settings UI writes; you can edit it directly and the adapters re-read it on the next request. ←PreviousNext→ 3Then the home patch⌄ `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` — cross-profile overrides. ←PreviousNext→ 4Then `--patch` overlays⌄ Command-line overlays, applied last. `config/examples/` ships opt-in overlays for GitHub review webhooks, memory MCP servers and runtime Cordis tools; they are never part of a default profile. ←PreviousNext→ 5Inspect before you boot⌄ `--dump-default-config` and `--dump-config` print the composed tree without starting anything — the fastest way to answer "which layer set this?" ←PreviousNext→ With HMR enabled in YAML, dsh-hmr watches the profile manifest and both patch files and recomposes every layer through one serialized reload. Without it, changes apply on restart.
documents.s: Configuration: five layers, and the override that eats your providers

documents.t: A Cordis config override replaces the complete entry config. The providers guide spells this out: when you edit an existing override, you must preserve the other fields and other providers yourself. Patch one provider carelessly and you have deleted the rest. This is the single most expensive mistake available in cordis.patch.yml. A Provider ID is permanent. Requests, saved sessions, model defaults and credential references all key off it. Renaming means adding a new provider and deleting the old one. Display name, base URL, protocol, credential and model list stay editable. --dump-config-schema imports plugin code. Unlike the other dump flags, it loads the composed tree's declared plugin schemas to print JSON Schema — so pointing it at untrusted plugins executes their import-time code. The CLI reference has a dedicated safety note on this. Treat it like reviewing third-party code, not like --help. Plugin version compatibility is enforced, and the escape hatch is explicit. Installation and profile startup check declared DSH peer ranges against the runtime version from dsh --version; an incompatible plugin requires an acknowledged exact-version exemption (allow-version, revoke-version). Good hygiene, surprising the first time a plugin refuses to load. A session that has already sent a request keeps the model recorded in its own log. Changing the default model does not retroactively move a live session, and if a saved default names a deleted provider the composer blocks input until you pick another. Both are correct behaviour; both look like bugs at 1 a.m.
documents.s: Five gotchas that will cost you an hour

documents.t: Start the Web UI, then a headless one-shot run — no clone, no build CopyOpen in Claude↗ # Web UI on http://127.0.0.1:3080, workspace defaults to the invoking directory npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web # One persisted session, final answer to stdout, then exit — the CI shape npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile headless "summarize this repo and list its main packages" # Serve automation clients over ACP stdio (editor integrations) npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile acp # Inspect the composed config tree WITHOUT booting it npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile web --dump-config # Manage a profile's plugins (forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory) npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add some-dsh-plugin Point dsh at a gateway that speaks Anthropic Messages — in $DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml CopyOpen in Claude↗ # WARNING: a Cordis config override replaces the ENTIRE entry config. # Include every provider you want to keep, not just the new one. - id: llm-pi-ai config: providers: my-anthropic-gateway: apiKeyEnv: GATEWAY_API_KEY api: anthropic-messages # or openai-completions / openai-responses baseURL: https://gateway.example/v1 models: - id: some-text-model - id: some-vision-model input: [text, image] # omit to inherit the catalog's input types Bring your Claude Code guardrails across CopyOpen in Claude↗ # The Claude Code hook bridge runs your existing command hooks inside dsh. # Only the command-hook subset documented by Claude Code is supported. # Hooks can: block a prompt or a tool call with a MODEL-VISIBLE message, # add conversation context, or require the run to continue. # # Check the bridge's own README for the current config field names before # wiring this up — the 0.2 line is a developer preview and they can move: # packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/README.md # # Verify enforcement the same way you would in Claude Code: a hook that is # configured but never fires is worse than no hook, because you trust it.

If you are choosing a harness rather than studying one, the honest summary is: dsh is the most architecturally interesting open harness shipping right now and the least ready to be load-bearing. Its own safety file says so. The plugin model is genuinely stronger than its competitors' — ctx.agentLoop being replaceable is not a thing you can do in most harnesses at any price — and the hook bridges mean adopting it is not an all-or-nothing bet. Against that: a release-candidate latest tag, no security audit, promised breaking changes, and a provider story that assumes API keys. For a comparison across the field, see coding agent CLIs compared and local coding agents. For the models you would most plausibly drive it with, see DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. 뒤집기용어DeepSeek Harness, in one line정의`dsh` — DeepSeek's open-source agent harness. MIT, TypeScript, first published 13 August 2026, 242,626 stars / 29,081 forks as of 2026-10-03. Start with `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.Enter 또는 스페이스 키를 눌러 카드를 뒤집습니다. 좌우 화살표 키로 카드를 이동할 수 있습니다.용어가 표시되었습니다. ←이전 1 / 15 다음→ Check yourself 0/7 1In DeepSeek Harness, which of these is NOT replaceable from configuration? The model adapterThe agent loopThe session logNone of them — architecture.md states all three are plugins 2You want to drive dsh with Claude using the subscription you already pay for. What happens? It works — pick the `anthropic` provider and sign inIt does not: OAuth sign-in providers are not supported, so you need an API keyIt works only in the `acp` profileIt works but requires the Anthropic Messages protocol to be set manually 3You edit `llm-pi-ai` in cordis.patch.yml to add one new gateway, listing only that gateway under `providers`. What is the result? The new gateway is merged alongside your existing providersThe edit is rejected because the config is incompleteYour other providers disappear — a Cordis override replaces the entire entry configThe new gateway is ignored until you restart dsh 4What does `workspace-write` actually rely on, on macOS? A container runtimeSeatbeltLandlockA restricted access token 5Why can dsh replay a session and measure its token cost? Because it caches every model responseBecause the session log guarantees that everything model-visible is loggedBecause the DeepSeek API returns deterministic outputsBecause token-meter re-tokenizes the rendered UI transcript 6You configure no MCP servers. What does the model see? A short MCP section explaining that no servers are connectedThe shared resource tools, with an empty server listNothing MCP-related at all — no prompt text and no tools, in native or PTC modeIt depends on the profile 7Which dump flag should you NOT point at untrusted plugins? `--dump-config``--dump-default-config``--dump-config-schema`All three are inert

deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness — the repository: README, star and fork counts, MIT licence, dsh-plugin topic. docs/architecture.md — the plugin claim, service keys, profiles and bundles, the turn/step loop, the session-log invariant. docs/cordis-primer.md — Cordis in five ideas, the five dispatch modes, waterfall semantics, loader configuration. docs/capability-seams.md — the generated service graph: every ctx.* key, its owner, implementations and consumers. SAFETY.md — what the harness can do to your machine, and the explicit "not secure or production-ready" statement. packages/sandbox/README.md — the three modes, the per-platform backends, escalation, and "same-world only". packages/hooks/README.md — the Claude Code and Codex hook bridges and the command-hook-subset limit. packages/ptc-runtime/README.md — the run_code contract, fresh-process execution, the experimental Python backend. docs/subsystems/mcp.md — per-server client plugins, scope rules, name namespacing, maxInstructionBytes, protocol negotiation. docs/user/guide/providers.md — provider ids, the three API protocols, OAuth limitation, credential storage, the override warning. apps/cli/README.md — entry modes, profile composition order, bundle names, dsh plugin, the dump flags, version exemptions. DeepSeek Harness product page — the desktop installers (macOS Apple Silicon .dmg, Windows 64-bit .exe) and the preview status. arXiv:2608.25512 — A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability, the Cordis paper the project cites. awesome-dsh-plugin — community plugin index for the dsh-plugin topic.

Pi 1.0: the minimal harness and the codemode trick — the clearest published account of why run_code saves context, and the MCP-exposure modes that go with it. Coding agent CLIs compared — where dsh sits against the harnesses you might already be running. Securing local and hybrid agents — what to put around any harness whose own safety file tells you not to trust its sandbox.

중급 오랫동안 "좋은 AI"에 대한 이야기는 API를 통해서만 빌려 쓸 수 있는 소수의 폐쇄형 프런티어 모델에 대한 이야기였습니다. 이제는 더 이상 그것이 이야기의 전부가 아닙니다. 오픈 웨이트 모델의 물결 — 상당수가 DeepSeek과 알리바바의 Qwen 같은 중국 연구소에서, 그리고 Meta의 Llama와 프랑스의 Mistral에서 나왔습니다 — 이 충분히 뛰어나고, 충분히 저렴하며, 충분히 작아져서 자신만의 유능한 모델을 다운로드해 직접 실행하는 것이 현실적인 선택지가 되었습니다. 이 페이지는 그 지형에 대한 변치 않는 지도입니다. 왜 이런 일이 일어났는지, "오픈 웨이트"가 실제로 무엇을 의미하는지, 폐쇄형 프런티어 모델과 비교했을 때의 솔직한 트레이드오프, 그리고 오늘날 이 모델들을 실제로 어떻게 사용하는지를 다룹니다. What you'll learn 오픈 웨이트 모델이 경쟁력을 갖추게 된 이유 이해하기 — 비용 대비 성능과 열린 추론 '오픈 웨이트'가 실제로 무엇을 의미하는지 정확히 파악하기 — 오픈 소스 대비, 오픈 데이터 대비 원형을 알아보기: 일반 챗, 추론, 코딩, 그리고 소형/효율 모델 폐쇄형 프런티어 대비 실제 트레이드오프 저울질하기 — 가장 어려운 작업에서의 성능 격차, 그리고 자체 인프라와 안전성을 스스로 소유하는 것 실제로 사용하는 두 가지 방법 알기: 호스팅 API, 또는 Ollama를 통한 셀프 호스팅
documents.s: DeepSeek, Qwen 그리고 오픈 웨이트의 물결

documents.t: 거의 같은 시기에 세 가지가 바뀌었고, 이들이 함께 일상적인 격차의 대부분을 좁혔습니다. 비용 대비 성능이 무너져 내렸습니다. 더 나은 학습 레시피, 데이터 큐레이션, 그리고 전문가 혼합(MoE) 아키텍처(대형 모델의 파라미터 중 일부만 토큰마다 활성화되는 방식) 덕분에 연구소들은 비용을 훨씬 웃도는 성능의 모델을 출시할 수 있게 되었습니다. 초안 작성, 요약, 추출, 분류, 일상적 코딩 같은 실제 작업의 상당수에서, 좋은 오픈 모델은 이제 프런티어 API 비용의 극히 일부로 "충분히 좋은" 수준입니다. 열린 추론 모델이 등장했습니다. DeepSeek의 추론 라인은 전환점이었습니다. "답하기 전에 단계별로 생각하는" 능력 — 이전에는 소수 폐쇄형 모델의 해자였던 — 이 오픈 웨이트로 학습되고 공개될 수 있음을 보여주었습니다. 한 연구소가 이를 입증하자, 나머지 오픈 생태계가 뒤따랐습니다. 소형 모델이 진짜로 쓸 만해졌습니다. 10B 미만, 심지어 1B 미만 모델도 일관되고 유용해졌으며, 이는 노트북이나 저렴한 서버에서도 유능한 무언가를 실행할 수 있다는 뜻입니다. 이는 프라이버시, 지연 시간, 규모의 경제학을 바꿉니다. 순효과: 폐쇄형 프런티어와의 격차가 사라진 것은 아니지만, 대부분의 작업에서 그것이 더 이상 결정적 요인이 아니게 되었습니다. 결정적 요인은 비용, 통제, 그리고 데이터가 어디에 위치하는가가 되었습니다.
documents.s: 오픈 웨이트 모델이 갑자기 경쟁력을 갖추게 된 이유

documents.t: 이것은 이 분야 전체에서 가장 자주 혼동되는 지점입니다. "오픈"이라는 단어는 서로 다른 세 가지 방식으로 많은 역할을 하고 있으며, 이들은 같은 것이 아닙니다. 용어 실제로 얻는 것 보통 얻지 못하는 것 오픈 웨이트 학습된 모델 파일(가중치). 다운로드, 실행, 파인튜닝, 셀프 호스팅이 가능합니다. 학습 데이터, 그리고 때로는 전체 학습 코드. 사용은 커스텀 라이선스의 규제를 받을 수 있습니다. 오픈 소스(엄격한 의미) 가중치 에 더해 OSI 스타일 라이선스로 제공되는 학습/추론 코드, 사용·수정·재배포의 자유. 여전히 학습 데이터는 대개 포함되지 않습니다. 오픈 데이터 모델이 학습된 실제 데이터셋을 공개적으로 게시한 것. 프런티어 규모 모델에서는 드뭅니다. 대부분의 "오픈" 모델은 오픈 데이터가 아니라 오픈 웨이트입니다. 실질적인 요점: 사람들이 "오픈 소스"라고 부르는 대부분의 모델은 사실 오픈 웨이트입니다. 실행하고 적응시킬 수는 있지만, 일반적으로 처음부터 재현할 수는 없으며, 라이선스를 반드시 읽어야 합니다. 라이선스는 다양합니다. 일부는 상업적 사용에 깔끔한 허용적 라이선스(Apache 2.0, MIT)로 제공됩니다 — 예를 들어 Qwen과 Mistral 모델은 역사적으로 Apache 2.0을 사용해 왔고, DeepSeek는 주요 릴리스에 MIT를 사용해 왔습니다. 일부는 조건이 붙은 커스텀 커뮤니티 라이선스로 제공됩니다 — 예를 들어 Meta의 Llama 라이선스는 역사적으로 (월간 활성 사용자 기준) 최대 규모 기업이 자유롭게 사용하는 것을 제한하는 조항을 포함해 왔습니다. 무언가를 그 위에 구축하기 전에 항상 해당 모델의 모델 카드에서 라이선스를 확인하세요. 중립적이지만 중요한 점: 모델이 오픈 웨이트라는 것은 당신이 직접 호스팅할 수 있다는 것을 알려줄 뿐, 법적 조건을 알려주지는 않으며, 라이선싱이나 데이터 거주지 문제를 사라지게 하지도 않습니다 — 그 문제를 당신에게 옮겨 놓을 뿐입니다. 최종 검증: 2026-06-28. 정확한 현재 모델 버전, 파라미터 수, 벤치마크 점수, 토큰당 가격은 빠르게 변하며, 여기서는 의도적으로 영구적인 사실로 단정하지 않습니다. 지형의 변치 않는 형태 — 연구소들, 원형들, 그리고 오픈 웨이트 대 오픈 소스 대 오픈 데이터의 구분 — 은 안정적이지만, 구체적인 리더보드 수치는 그렇지 않습니다. 현재 무엇이 최신인지는 링크된 조직 페이지에서 확인하세요. 다음에서 확인하세요: 공식 출처.

오픈 웨이트 계열은 거의 항상 단일 모델이 아니라 변형의 스펙트럼으로 나옵니다. 네 가지 원형을 익히면 어떤 연구소의 라인업이든 한눈에 읽을 수 있습니다. 오픈 웨이트 모델 원형 뒤집기용어일반 챗 / 인스트럭트정의만능형: 대화, 글쓰기, 요약, 폭넓은 Q&A를 위한 인스트럭션 튜닝 모델. 특화된 필요가 없을 때의 기본 출발점. (예: 기본 Qwen / Llama / Mistral 인스트럭트 모델, DeepSeek-V 시리즈.)Enter 또는 스페이스 키를 눌러 카드를 뒤집습니다. 좌우 화살표 키로 카드를 이동할 수 있습니다.용어가 표시되었습니다. ←이전 1 / 4 다음→ 단일 계열 — Qwen이 가장 명확한 예입니다 — 은 일반적으로 전체 사다리를 제공합니다: 엣지와 노트북용 초소형 모델, 서버용 중형 모델, 가장 어려운 작업을 위한 대형 플래그십, 그리고 코딩 및 추론에 특화된 변형들. 당신은 "그 모델"이 아니라 자신의 하드웨어와 작업에 맞는 단을 고릅니다.

오픈 웨이트 모델은 단순한 업그레이드가 아닙니다. 다른 거래입니다. 그 거래를 중립적으로 정리하면 다음과 같습니다. 차원 오픈 웨이트(셀프 호스팅 또는 저렴한 호스팅) 폐쇄형 프런티어(호스팅 API) 가장 어려운 작업의 성능 강력하고 빠르게 좁혀지고 있지만, 폐쇄형 프런티어가 여전히 가장 어려운 추론, 장기 지평 에이전트, 틈새 작업에서 보통 앞섭니다 일반적으로 가장 까다로운 작업에서 천장 역할 규모에서의 비용 특히 셀프 호스팅이나 저예산 호스팅을 통하면 극적으로 저렴할 수 있음 토큰당 프리미엄; 예측 가능하지만 쌓이면 부담 프라이버시 / 데이터 거주지 데이터를 자신의 환경 안에 완전히 유지할 수 있음 데이터가 당신의 네트워크를 떠나 제공자에게 감 통제 및 커스터마이징 완전함: 파인튜닝, 양자화, 버전 고정, 오프라인 실행 API가 노출하는 것에 한정됨; 버전이 당신 모르게 바뀔 수 있음 안전성과 운영의 소유자 당신 — 가드레일, 남용 필터링, 가동 시간, 확장, 패치가 당신의 일 제공자가 인프라를 운영하고 기본 안전성을 제공 그 마지막 행이 사람들이 과소평가하는 부분입니다. 오픈 웨이트 모델을 셀프 호스팅하면, 보통 프런티어 연구소가 당신을 대신해 떠안아 주던 책임도 함께 물려받습니다: 콘텐츠 안전성과 남용 완화, 배포의 패치 유지, 용량과 가동 시간, 그리고 새 모델 버전마다 스스로 평가하기. "오픈 웨이트"는 당신에게 통제를 사 주지만, 통제는 이득인 만큼이나 비용이기도 합니다. 이 거래의 API 측 비용 직관에 대해서는 토큰 경제를 참고하세요.

정확히 두 가지 경로가 있으며, 대부분의 팀은 서로 다른 단계에서 둘 다 사용합니다. 호스팅 API — 많은 제공자(연구소 자체와 서드파티 추론 호스트를 포함해)가 오픈 웨이트 모델을 API 뒤에서, 종종 OpenAI 호환 방식으로 제공합니다. 인프라 작업 제로로 오픈 모델의 경제성을 얻습니다. 서버를 운영하지 않으면서 낮은 비용을 원할 때 가장 좋지만, 데이터가 여전히 당신의 네트워크를 떠난다는 점에 유의하세요. 셀프 호스팅 — 가중치를 다운로드해 자신의 환경에서 실행합니다. 최대의 프라이버시와 통제, 그리고 데이터가 정말로 네트워크를 떠날 수 없을 때의 유일한 선택지입니다. 가장 쉬운 진입로는 Ollama로, 명령어 하나로 오픈 모델을 가져와 실행합니다.

Guided walkthrough1 of 4 1Ollama 설치⌄ ollama.com/download에서 다운로드(macOS/Windows)하거나 Linux 설치 스크립트를 사용하세요. 이렇게 하면 ollama 명령어와 로컬 백그라운드 서비스가 생깁니다. 전체 설명은 로컬에서 모델 실행하기 페이지에 있습니다. ←PreviousNext→ 2당신의 기기가 돌릴 수 있는 크기 고르기⌄ 작은 모델일수록 더 적은 RAM/VRAM이 필요합니다. 노트북은 소형 변형(몇 GB)을 편안하게 실행하며, 대형 플래그십은 진짜 GPU나 서버가 필요합니다. 모든 것이 작동하는지 확인하려면 작게 시작하고, 품질이 충분하지 않으면 규모를 키우세요. ←PreviousNext→ 3명령어 하나로 실행하기⌄ ollama run <model>은 처음 사용 시 가중치를 다운로드(수 GB)한 다음, 대화형 챗으로 안내합니다. 첫 실행은 가져오는 중이라 느리고, 이후 실행은 캐시에서 즉시 시작됩니다. ←PreviousNext→ 4코드에서 호출하기⌄ Ollama는 OpenAI 호환 로컬 엔드포인트를 노출하므로, 기존 OpenAI 스타일 SDK를 클라우드 대신 localhost로 가리킬 수 있습니다. 이제 같은 코드가 비공개 로컬 모델을 상대로 실행됩니다. ←PreviousNext→ Ollama로 오픈 모델을 로컬에서 가져와 실행하기 CopyOpen in Claude↗ ollama run qwen3 그 명령어 하나가 Qwen 오픈 웨이트 모델을 다운로드하고 로컬 챗을 시작합니다 — API 키 없이, 데이터가 당신의 기기를 떠나지 않고. qwen3를 다른 계열(예를 들어 Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek 태그)로 바꿔서 자신의 작업에서 비교해 보세요. 주어진 일에 맞는 모델을 고르는 것은 그 자체로 하나의 기술입니다: 모델 선택하기를 참고하세요.

리더보드로 고르지 마세요. 제약으로 고르세요: 데이터가 네트워크를 떠날 수 없음 → 셀프 호스팅 오픈 웨이트가 답입니다, 두말할 것 없이. 대용량, 비용 민감, "충분히 좋은" 품질 → 오픈 웨이트(호스팅 또는 셀프 호스팅)가 보통 비용에서 이깁니다. 가장 어려운 작업에서 절대적 최고가 필요함 → 폐쇄형 프런티어가 여전히 앞서는 경향이 있습니다 — 중요한 곳에 사용하고 더 쉬운 트래픽은 더 저렴한 오픈 모델로 라우팅하세요. 파인튜닝, 양자화, 버전 고정, 또는 오프라인 실행을 원함 → 오픈 웨이트만이 그 통제를 제공합니다. 가장 변치 않는 방법은 당신 자신의 실제 데이터로 오픈 후보 하나와 폐쇄 후보 하나에 대해 소규모 평가를 돌려 보는 것입니다. 벤치마크는 다른 누군가의 작업을 설명하고, 당신의 평가는 당신의 작업을 설명합니다. 스스로 점검하기 0/3 1'오픈 웨이트'는 당신이 무엇을 얻는다는 것을 보장하나요? 모델이 학습한 학습 데이터셋실행하고 파인튜닝할 수 있는 다운로드 가능한 학습된 모델 파일아무 조건도 없는 허용적 라이선스 2법적으로 네트워크를 떠날 수 없는 데이터를 처리해야 합니다. 어떤 경로가 맞나요? 호스팅 API를 통한 폐쇄형 프런티어 모델자신의 환경에서 셀프 호스팅하는 오픈 웨이트 모델OpenAI 호환이기만 하면 어떤 호스팅 API든 3오픈 웨이트 모델을 셀프 호스팅할 때 당신이 새로 떠안는 책임은 무엇인가요? 없음 — 호스팅 API와 완전히 똑같이 동작함안전 가드레일, 가동 시간, 확장, 패치가 당신의 몫이 됨파인튜닝한 가중치를 공개적으로 게시해야 함 Key takeaways 오픈 웨이트 모델은 비용 대비 성능, 열린 추론 모델, 그리고 진짜로 쓸 만한 소형 모델 덕분에 일상적인 격차의 대부분을 좁혔습니다 '오픈 웨이트' = 실행하고 파인튜닝할 수 있는 다운로드 가능한 가중치 — 반드시 오픈 소스 코드, 오픈 학습 데이터, 허용적 라이선스를 뜻하지는 않습니다; 항상 모델 카드를 읽으세요 어떤 라인업이든 원형으로 읽으세요: 일반 챗, 추론, 코딩, 소형/효율 — 대부분의 계열은 전체 크기 사다리를 제공합니다 거래는 실재합니다: 오픈은 비용, 프라이버시, 통제를 사 주지만, 폐쇄형 프런티어가 여전히 가장 어려운 작업에서 보통 앞서고 당신은 안전성과 인프라를 물려받습니다 사용하는 두 가지 방법: 호스팅(종종 OpenAI 호환) API, 또는 명령어 하나로 Ollama를 통한 셀프 호스팅 — 그런 다음 리더보드가 아니라 당신의 데이터로 평가하세요

중급 At 04:00 UTC on September 10, 2026, DeepSeek flipped its API to a new model and published the weights the same day: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, served as deepseek-flash. It is the smallest member of a new architecture family, but it is not a small model: 552 billion parameters, a 1-million-token context, native vision, and a KV cache that costs 890 bytes per token. On DeepSWE v1.1, the long-horizon software-engineering benchmark both Google and Anthropic now headline, DeepSeek reports 74.2, one-fifth of a point above Claude Opus 5. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 it reports 31.2 against Opus 5's 51.8. Both numbers are true, and the gap between them is the whole story. This page is the field guide for a Claude user: what actually changed, the routing change that quietly re-pointed every deepseek-v4-pro request, the effort dial and what it does to your bill, how to run the weights, and the workloads where Claude is still the right call. What you'll learn Read the V4.1-Flash launch numbers the way they deserve: tied with Opus 5 on DeepSWE, far behind on Terminal-Bench, and why that split is not a contradiction Understand the new Causal Encoder-Decoder + CSA2 design well enough to know what the 890-byte KV cache buys you (and what DeepSeek says it has not yet characterized) Use the 1–100 reasoning_effort dial deliberately — 25 vs 100 is an 8-point DeepSWE swing for ~2.5× the output tokens Do the honest cost math: $0.30 / $1.20 peak, half that off-peak, $0.003 per million on an off-peak cache hit — and the UTC peak window that decides which rate you pay Know the September 14 routing change: deepseek-v4-pro now silently serves V4.1-Flash until V4.1-Pro ships Pick a serving path (hosted API, vLLM, SGLang, Docker Model Runner) and the sampling defaults DeepSeek recommends 최종 검증: 2026-09-15. Model ID, routing dates, and pricing from DeepSeek's September 10 announcement and the API pricing page. Architecture, license, reasoning-effort range, and sampling defaults from the Hugging Face model card. Benchmark comparisons against Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol are DeepSeek's own launch table as reported by VentureBeat on September 10; treat them as vendor-run until an independent harness publishes. The 3.0/4.0 Terminal-Bench gaps come from the same table. DeepSeek's statement that the architecture has "robustness boundaries it has not fully characterized" is quoted from the same coverage. 다음에서 확인하세요: 공식 출처.

documents.t: V4.1-Flash is DeepSeek's first model on a new architecture (a "Causal Encoder-Decoder" with Compressed Sparse Attention 2), released MIT-licensed with native vision, a 1M-token window, 384K max output, and a continuously controllable reasoning effort from 1 to 100. It replaces every V4-era Flash endpoint immediately and, since September 14, also answers every deepseek-v4-pro call at Flash prices until V4.1-Pro lands.

DeepSeek's launch table, in the columns that matter for an agent shop: Benchmark DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Claude Opus 5 GPT-5.6 Sol DeepSWE v1.1 (resolved) 74.2 74.0 73.0 Terminal-Bench 3.0 30.0 43.3 — Terminal-Bench 4.0 31.2 51.8 — CyberGym 88.1 — — AutomationBench 54.8 — — DeepSWE rewards a model that reads a repository, plans a patch, and lands it: long context, careful retrieval, a few large edits. Terminal-Bench rewards many short, adaptive shell turns where each decision depends on the last tool result. V4.1-Flash has 1M tokens of context and a cheap cache, so the first shape suits it. It runs 8B active parameters per token at prefill and 16B at decode, which is a lot less "thinking per step" than a dense frontier model, so the second shape hurts. If your work looks like a pull request, the parity claim is credible and worth an eval. If your work looks like an interactive terminal session, the 20-point Terminal-Bench gap is the number to budget around. The same split shows up in Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash launch a week earlier, and for the same architectural reasons. The base-model rows tell a quieter story: MMLU-Pro 74.1 (V4-Flash 68.3, V4-Pro 73.5), HumanEval 79.4 (V4-Flash 69.5), GSM8K 93.0 (V4-Flash 90.8). The new "Flash" is a better base than last month's "Pro", which is why DeepSeek was comfortable routing Pro traffic onto it.
documents.s: 1. DeepSWE parity and Terminal-Bench deficit are the same fact seen twice

documents.t: Unlike Claude's effort (low/medium/high/max), V4.1-Flash exposes an integer from 1 to 100. DeepSeek's own ablation on DeepSWE v1.1: effort 25 scores 66.0%, effort 100 scores 74.2%, and the top setting emits roughly 2.5× as many output tokens. They also say the 60–80 band delivers most of the maximum-effort accuracy at less than half the token budget. Every benchmark row above was run at reasoning_effort=100. So the parity number is the expensive number. Reproduce it at 100 first, then walk down to the cheapest setting your evals still pass at. That is the same discipline we recommend for thinking_level on Gemini and effort on Claude in Reasoning models compared.
documents.s: 2. The reasoning-effort dial is a real dial, and it is on your bill

documents.t: From September 10, deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp route to V4.1-Flash, billed at Flash rates. The V4-Flash-Vision-Exp page's numbers now describe the open weights, not the hosted endpoint. From 04:00 UTC September 14, every deepseek-v4-pro request also routes to V4.1-Flash at Flash rates, "until V4.1-Pro launches". If you have evals pinned to deepseek-v4-pro, your production model changed under you on Sunday morning. Re-run the suite. The upside is that the same call now costs roughly a quarter of the Pro rate; the downside is that any Pro-specific behavior you tuned for is gone. This is exactly the failure mode Porting prompts across models warns about when a provider aliases model IDs.
documents.s: 3. Two routing changes happened without a client-side change

documents.t: Spec DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash API model ID deepseek-flash Release September 10, 2026 (API + open weights same day) Parameters 552B total; 8B active at prefill, 16B at decode MoE layout 384 routed + 1 shared expert per MoE layer; 6 routed experts active per token Architecture Causal Encoder-Decoder, Compressed Sparse Attention 2 (CSA2) KV cache 890 bytes per token (FP4, E2M1): ~1/4 of V4-Flash in HBM, ~1/8 in SSD storage; global KV cache lifetime at least 72 hours Context / max output 1M tokens / 384K tokens Vision Native; DeepSeek-ViT trained from scratch, 2D-RoPE, 3×3 pixel-unshuffle downsampling Reasoning control reasoning_effort integer 1–100 License MIT Weights Safetensors in BF16, F32, F8_E4M3, I8 Serving vLLM, SGLang, Docker Model Runner, Transformers; reference inference code in the inference/ folder Recommended sampling temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 or 1.0, context 1M API concurrency 2,500 The KV-cache line is the architectural headline. A 1M-token conversation at 890 bytes per token is under a gigabyte of cache, which is why DeepSeek can promise a 72-hour cache lifetime and price cache hits at fractions of a cent. Anthropic's answer to the same problem is a cheaper cache-read rate on Claude Fable 5.1; DeepSeek's is to make the cache physically small. Both push you toward the same habit: put the stable prefix first and never edit it mid-run. See Prompt caching.

DeepSeek keeps a two-rate schedule. Peak hours are 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday; everything else is off-peak at exactly half the peak rate. Per 1M tokens Peak Off-peak Input, cache hit $0.006 $0.003 Input, cache miss $0.30 $0.15 Output $1.20 $0.60 Two things follow. First, the "$0.003 per million" headline is the off-peak cache-hit price, the cheapest of six cells; a cold, peak-hour agent run pays 100× that on input. Second, the peak window is defined in UTC and covers the European morning and the tail of the U.S. night. A batch job scheduled at 09:00 UTC pays double what the same job pays at 11:00 UTC. If you can shift, shift. For a framework that puts these cells beside Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google list prices, use What AI costs across providers; current Claude list prices live on Models and pricing.

Hosted is right for almost everyone: the model is enormous, and the API is the cheapest thing on this page. Self-host when data cannot leave your network or when you want the effort dial and 1M window without a rate limit. Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Decide hosted vs self-hosted honestly⌄ 552B parameters in BF16 is over a terabyte of weights; the F8_E4M3 and I8 safetensors halve or quarter that but still need a multi-GPU node. If you do not already run Kimi K3 or Colibrì-class MoEs, the hosted endpoint at $0.30 / $1.20 peak will beat your amortized hardware bill. See the hardware math on Running Kimi K3 locally. ←PreviousNext→ 2Pick a serving stack the card actually names⌄ vLLM, SGLang, Docker Model Runner, and Transformers are the four listed. The card ships no Jinja chat template; it uses a custom encoding implementation, so use the reference code in the repo's inference folder (or the deepseek-recipe toolkit) rather than hand-rolling the prompt format. ←PreviousNext→ 3Set the sampling defaults DeepSeek recommends⌄ temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 or 1.0, context window 1M. These are the settings the benchmark rows were produced with. Do not port a Claude-tuned temperature of 0.2 over blindly. ←PreviousNext→ 4Start at reasoning_effort=100, then walk down⌄ Reproduce DeepSeek's number on your own eval first. Then try 80, 60, 40 and record accuracy vs output tokens. Most teams will land in the 60–80 band the vendor itself points at. ←PreviousNext→ 5Test long-context retrieval before you trust it⌄ DeepSeek says the new architecture has robustness boundaries it has not fully characterized, specifically sparse retrieval over very long contexts. Run a needle-in-haystack and a multi-hop retrieval test at the context length you will actually use. Treat the 1M number as a ceiling, not a promise. ←PreviousNext→ Hosted call with the effort dial (OpenAI-compatible endpoint) CopyOpen in Claude↗ curl https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "deepseek-flash", "reasoning_effort": 70, "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a senior engineer. Reply with a unified diff and one paragraph of rationale."}, {"role": "user", "content": "The test suite in ./tests fails on macOS only. Here is the log and the relevant module: ..."} ] }' Self-hosted with vLLM (shape only; check the model card for the exact flags) CopyOpen in Claude↗ # One node, tensor-parallel across all visible GPUs. # The card names vLLM, SGLang, Docker Model Runner and Transformers as supported. vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --max-model-len 1000000 \ --trust-remote-code # Then hit http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions with the same body as above.

Pro tip Reach for V4.1-Flash: repository-scale coding tasks that look like DeepSWE (read a lot, edit a little), where you can run at effort 60–100 and the cost per resolved issue still undercuts Claude by an order of magnitude. Reach for V4.1-Flash: anything that needs a 1M-token window and a warm cache for days — a 72-hour global cache lifetime and 890-byte-per-token KV make 'keep the whole codebase in context' cheap. Reach for V4.1-Flash: self-hosted or data-residency workloads where MIT licensing matters and you already run a multi-GPU MoE stack. Stay on Claude: interactive terminal agents and any many-short-turns loop. A 20-point Terminal-Bench 4.0 gap (31.2 vs 51.8) is not noise, and it is the shape of most real Claude Code sessions. Stay on Claude: work that needs Anthropic's tool-use loop, prefilled assistant turns, structured-output strictness, or the safety and retention guarantees of a first-party API. The DeepSeek API is OpenAI-shaped and the model has documented, uncharacterized long-context failure modes. Cross-check both: for a coding agent, run your own eval at DeepSeek's effort=100 and Claude's default effort, then at the cheapest passing setting on each. The vendor tables were run at maximum effort; your bill will not be. For the durable framework behind that list, How to choose a model. For what changes when you move a prompt between an Anthropic-shaped and an OpenAI-shaped API, Porting prompts across models. For the Claude-side reference these comparisons hang off, Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.
documents.s: When to reach for V4.1-Flash, and when to stay on Claude

Match it to work that reads a lot and edits a little. The 1–100 effort dial is the price lever. Two silent routing changes: V4-Flash endpoints on Sept 10, deepseek-v4-pro on Sept 14. If you pinned Pro, your model changed — re-run evals. The 890-byte KV cache and 72-hour cache lifetime make long-lived 1M-token contexts cheap, but DeepSeek itself flags long-context sparse retrieval as uncharacterized. Test before you trust.

중급 At 00:00 UTC on August 31, 2026, DeepSeek quietly pushed a new repository to Hugging Face: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp. Ten days after the same model went live on their API (August 21), the weights are now MIT-licensed and public. This is the first V4-family model with native vision — not a text model with a bolt-on adapter, but a joint-trained multimodal MoE — and its agent scores on the vision side jumped from 26.2 to 36.5 on ApexBench without moving the text-only agent scores at all. On several agent benchmarks it now matches or edges past Claude Opus 4.8 while the API costs $0.22 per million input tokens. This page is the practical field guide the launch didn't come with: what changed architecturally, the numbers that matter, the one hard limit nobody warns you about, how to run it, and when Claude is still the right call. What you'll learn Understand what 'native vision' means here — the V4-Flash backbone plus a vision encoder + aligner trained together, not stapled on after Read the benchmark table the way the release intends: text-only agents preserved, vision agents up sharply, both within striking distance of Claude Opus 4.8 Know the hard 384-tokens-per-image architectural cap and why it changes how you prompt Do the honest cost math: $0.22 / $0.66 / $0.007 (cached) per million tokens vs Claude Opus 4.8 at $15 / $75 Pick the right serving path — hosted API for almost everyone, vLLM + DSpark for a real self-hosted run

documents.t: DeepSeek V4-Flash-Vision-Exp is a 305-billion-parameter sparse-MoE multimodal model — 13B active per token, 1.048M-token context — that adds joint-trained vision to the V4-Flash text backbone, ships open under MIT on Hugging Face on August 31 2026, and delivers agent-tier multimodal performance at roughly one-fortieth of Claude Opus 4.8's per-token price.

Every open lab that has bolted vision onto a strong text model has paid a tax on text benchmarks. DeepSeek's release table is the flex: on Terminal Bench 2.1 the vision model scores 83.9 (vs 82.7 for the text-only V4-Flash-0731); on DeepSWE it climbs to 59.3 (from 54.4); on Toolathlon-Verified to 75.9 (from 70.3). None of these are vision tasks — they're pure code and tool-use agent evals. The vision variant is better on text-agent work than the text-only checkpoint, not worse. This matters because it's the "prove-out" the field has been waiting for since Chameleon: you can jointly train a giant MoE for text and vision without the multimodal add causing text regression, as long as the vision head lands late enough and the router gets to keep specializing text experts.
documents.s: 1. Vision was added without breaking the text agents — that's the whole point

documents.t: This is the single most important thing to learn before writing your first prompt. The vision encoder in V4-Flash-Vision-Exp allocates at most 384 tokens per image — and that ceiling is architectural, not a commercial policy. There is no "high-detail" mode that unlocks more. Practical consequences: Big screenshots lose fine text. A 2560×1440 dashboard, a dense CSV rendered as an image, or a long PDF page will be encoded at whatever resolution 384 tokens of visual features can express — meaning small-font text will not survive round-trip. Crop, don't scale. If you need to read numbers off a chart, send the chart cropped to the region of interest, not the whole page. Multi-image beats one giant image. Split large documents into per-region tiles; each tile gets its own 384-token budget. This is why Chartography lands at 64.3 (competitive with Claude Opus 4.8's 65.0) but why the model will still miss a footnote in a 12-point font on a full-page screenshot. Every vision-agent workflow you build should assume this ceiling. 최종 검증: 2026-09-01. 이 페이지에는 시간이 지나면 바뀌는 사실이 인용되어 있습니다 — 위의 날짜를 최신성의 기준으로 삼으세요. 다음에서 확인하세요: 공식 출처.
documents.s: 2. The vision encoder has a hard 384-tokens-per-image budget

documents.t: Most published MoE recipes activate 8 experts of 32 or 64. V4-Flash-Vision-Exp uses a much wider expert bank: 256 routed experts + 1 shared expert, with only 6 routed experts firing per token — a 2.3% activation ratio. The model has 43 layers, hidden size 4,096, and the hybrid attention stack combines two mechanisms: Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) — sparse patterns for long-range reads. Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA) — an aggressively compressed form for the deep-context tail. Wrapped over that, Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) replace the standard residual with a constrained-manifold projection, which the paper reports stabilizes signal propagation through the 43-layer stack. Together these are the reason the model can advertise a 1,048,576-token context window without the quadratic attention bill.
documents.s: 3. The MoE routing is unusually sparse — 6 of 256 experts fire per token

documents.t: Sticker prices, all per million tokens: Model Input Output Cached read DeepSeek V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (API) $0.22 $0.66 $0.007 Claude Opus 4.8 $15.00 $75.00 $1.50 Kimi K3 (cache-miss / cache-hit) $3.00 / $0.30 $15.00 $0.30 Cached-read at $0.007/M is not a typo — that is roughly one two-hundredth of a cent per thousand tokens. For any workload where a repeating system prompt or long context is re-sent (agent loops, RAG over a static corpus, chat with a fixed persona) the effective input price collapses. This is the reason V4-Flash-Vision-Exp is showing up in agent-cost tables at a fraction of what Claude Opus 4.8 costs per task, even when the raw quality is within a few points. 최종 검증: 2026-09-01.
